title: Around the house
description: Name the furniture, and use the plural when there is more than one.
grammar: gender and articles, and the plural of nouns
grammarNote: The plural is easy: add -s or -es to the noun, and change el and la to los and las.

explanation.summary: Furniture is a closed list of nouns, and every one of them needs its article. This unit also does the work of the plural, because a room rarely has only one chair.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El sofá, el sillón and el biombo are masculine. La estantería, la cómoda, la repisa and la alfombra are feminine. La planta is a nice one to know: it means both the plant and the floor of a building, and the context tells you which one you mean.

sections.heading: More than one
sections.body: The plural of a noun adds -s, or -es when the noun ends in a vowel: el sillón becomes los sillones and la planta becomes las plantas. The articles change too: el becomes los and la becomes las. So one sofa is el sofá, and two sofas are los sofás.

items.note: Masculine: el sofá. The plural is los sofás.
Masculine: el sillón. The plural is los sillones.
Feminine: la planta. It also means the floor of a building.
Feminine: la alfombra. The plural is las alfombras.

drills.meaning: the chest of drawers is made of wood
two armchairs in the living room
drills.note: A noun ending in a vowel adds -es.
Planta is feminine, so las plantas.
